## Summary
A 2-year-8-month live experiment in copy-trading US politician disclosures. When Nancy Pelosi disclosed a >$1.5M Nvidia call-options position (50 calls at ≈$38K each), the author bought exactly **one** of the same calls with $38,000. Within ~3 months both positions nearly tripled. The tweet is truncated mid-story ("My $38k …") — the full thread on X carries the rest of the log.

## Why it matters
- The claimed edge is **informational** (timely disclosure scraping of a famous politician), not analytical — a different risk profile from strategy-driven trading.
- Position-sizing trick worth remembering: match the *unit* (1 call), not the portfolio weight — lets a small account track a whale with defined risk.
- Survivorship caveat: one winning copy is an anecdote; the 32-month frame implies a longer log in the thread worth a skim if this angle gets interesting.
